text:
Sam L: Quick heads-up — platform is rolling out the ‘routing-policy’ gating change tomorrow for policy-based quota enforcement. If the SDKs don't surface a route policy header, the request will be routed to the default tier which may hit stricter quotas.
Elaine D: Wait — tomorrow? I thought we had a phased soft-fail for client libs. When did hard default go live?
Sam L: We discussed soft-fail, but ops found too many corner cases where the fallback ends up causing silent throttles. Decision was to make server enforce default mapping explicitly to avoid silent regressions.
Anya K: We need a clear SDK plan. TS+Py currently accept route hints via metadata; Go is still using raw headers. We should standardize an API param instead of forcing everyone to manipulate headers.
Raj P: Agree. Proposal: add optional param `routePolicy` to top-level request object in all SDKs and map that to `x-redwood-route-policy` header. Deprecate manual header usage but keep it supported for one release.
Elaine D: Sounds good. UX question: console showed a new per-route dropdown labelled “preferred routing profile” — will that map to the same values? (latency, cost, isolation)
Sam L: Yes, console values -> policy enum: `LATENCY`, `ECONOMY`, `ISOLATED`. We'll publish the mapping in the API changelog.
Anya K: For TS SDK: suggested signature change (non-breaking): `client.generate(input, {routePolicy?: 'LATENCY'|'ECONOMY'|'ISOLATED'})`. If omitted, we send no header during deprecation period. After cutoff we'll send `ECONOMY` as server default if absent.
Raj P: For Go it will be similar: add field to `RequestOptions` struct and helper `WithRoutePolicy(opt, policy)`. We'll also emit a deprecation log if manual header used.
Elaine D: Python needs to be careful about keyword arg name collisions. Maybe `routing_policy` to follow snake_case. Also we should update examples in quickstarts and notebook templates.
Sam L: Can we include a short snippet for docs?
Anya K: Sure — here's sample snippets I'll add to the SDK PRs:
```python
# python
resp = client.generate("Summarize...", routing_policy="LATENCY")
```
```ts
// typescript
await client.generate("Summarize...", { routePolicy: 'LATENCY' })
```
```go
// go
req := inference.Request{Input: "...", Options: inference.RequestOptions{RoutePolicy: inference.LATENCY}}
```
Sam L: Nice. Ops ask for telemetry: add `route_policy` to span attributes and to the usage event so console can break down cost/latency by policy. Devex: can you coordinate telemetry naming?
Elaine D: Will do — we'll use `routing.policy` for tracing attribute and `route_policy` for billing event to keep parity with existing dashboards.
Raj P: Migration plan idea: Day 0 (tomorrow) enforce default mapping server-side + emit metric for untagged requests. Day 7 start warning headers (429? no, only warnings in response body). Day 21 deprecate implicit mapping and require SDKs to send header or param.
Sam L: Ops wants quicker lock if we see spikes. We should add an admin kill-switch and rollout flag.
Anya K: For SDKs: I'll open TS/Go/PY PRs today with feature flags behind `enableRoutingPolicyParam=true` and add telemetry counters when codepath used. Keep tests minimal but add e2e in the internal integration harness.
Elaine D: I'll update quickstarts, console docs, and add a short paragraph in the release notes about deprecation window + example migration diff.
devex-bot: Reminder: create RFC doc in /docs with mapping table and include in release notes. (action: @Elaine D)
Sam L: Thanks all — please tag me on PRs. If anyone hits blockers ping me and we can extend timelines for SDK rollout. :thumbsup:
